notes.decision: Translated 'purpose of heart' per accumulated vocabulary, here in cosmic-architectural register: the entire 'inclination/intent' of the Gate is invested in a single object.
Translated 'gleam' (Crum: shine, gleam). The lighter sense fits the pairing with ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ (the Radiance).

Transliterated 'the prochos.' Etymology unclear — possibly Greek πρόχοος ('pitcher, outpouring') or προχοή/πρόοχος ('projection') used as a Manichaean technical term. The structure: contains 12 seals, archons, all firmaments, spheres, stars, all powers; stretched out before the Great Gate of Honor; explicitly likened to 'a great mirror' (line 31). It is the cosmic mirror-vault that displays/contains the entire archonic order.

Provisionally rendered 'their [...]' — the segmentation is opaque. Possible parsings: ⲧⲉϩⲙ̄-ⲡⲡⲉ ('in their heaven,' with ⲡⲡⲉ = Lyc. ⲡⲏⲩⲉ), or a compound noun. Translation tentative; sense flagged as uncertain.
Translated 'the five Men of Radiance' — ⲡⲉϩⲧⲟⲩ = ⲡⲉ-ϯⲟⲩ ('the five'); ⲣⲙⲙⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ = ⲣⲙ̄- ('men of') + ⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ ('Radiance'). Capitalized 'Radiance' per terminology guide.

Read as ⲡⲓ-ⲱⲡ 'this counting/this reckoning' (demonstrative + nominalized ⲱⲡ 'count'); fits the cosmological inventory-context of the previous lines (sealings, archons, firmaments all enumerated within the prochos). The 'counting' is what is 'stretched out at every hour' over against the Gate.
Translated 'no peering forth' per accumulated vocab ⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'peep forth, peer out.' The chain of fruit prevents any glimpse out from within.

Read as Greek loanword ἅλυσις ('chain') with prosthetic ⲍ-, fitting the immediate context (chain of their fruit / like a chain before the Archphylax) and the Lycopolitan ⲍ-onset for Greek aspirated forms (cf. ⲍⲉⲣⲙⲏⲛⲉⲩⲉ).
Read as ⲁ-prosthetic + κρίσις = 'the judgment.' The prochos as great mirror manifests/reveals all the archonic deeds for judgment — a Manichaean cosmic-tribunal motif.
